title: First music: tailgate wagons, bread-box drumming, Cooperators Hall bands
summary: He first heard advertising-truck jazz and drummed on bread boxes; living by Cooperators Hall he heard the great bands and sneaked out to listen.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: What was the first music you remember hearing when you were a kid? Parades? The parades?

No, it wasn't the parades. It was these advertisements that the bands on the truck, the tailgate music, was the first music that I heard, this jazz music like that. And we used to sit on the corner, they had bread boxes, the groceries. The bread man used to leave the bread in the box in the morning. And we used to take sticks and beat on the bread boxes because it sounds something like a drum.
How much then, your brother is older than you? Yeah, my brother is three years older than I am. My brother should be 50 now. So, oh man. Okay. So you started out as a drummer.
Yeah, I first wanted to play drums, you know. But, I don't know, I never did get around to it that much. So, finally my mother, later on my mother moved right next door to the old cooperators hall.
Oh yeah. That's the same way they call Hope's Hall. Yeah.
And that's where I heard all these great jazz bands like Chris Kelly, Guy Kelly, Papa Celestan, Kid Renee, and Manuel Perez.
Buddy Petit. Yeah, I heard all that. I heard, when I was small also, I heard Louis Armstrong's but it was in Perez.
I got a many whippers at night when they'd have these balls at the cooperators hall, you know. At that time, nine o'clock children had to be in bed.

And I'd sneak out and try to listen up to the band. My mother would miss me and fan me good. Yeah. But that's where I really began to love that music. But it wasn't then that I got the idea of playing music.
